items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: My personal opinion, and also that of Martin Williams, is that at least Steady Roll is without Morton.

ctx.x: M-O-R-E, yeah. Well, I think this way about it. Jelly could spell, see. Yeah. Jelly could spell and he could write. And if he wanted to be Frog Eye, F-R-O-G-G-I-E, he would have spelled it to him. I think that's right. But he just did the other thing. And he wrote that in 1918, and he didn't go out to the Pacific Coast after that until 1923 when he got mixed up with Benjamin Seitz. I don't know. I always say that name wrong, whatever it is.

I notice in here, there's a notation. Spikes, that's it. One record by Jelly Roll Morton's Stomp Kings, recorded in Chicago on April 1924, Steady Roll, issued on Paramount and other labels, issued on Riverside. According to Thomas Cusack's Jelly Roll Morton discography, these two titles are without jelly. Nevertheless, the Riverside Record Company has included them as Morton items in their History of Jazz series. My personal opinion, and also that of Martin Williams, is that at least Steady Roll is without Morton.

Oh, yeah. Steady Roll is not in the History of Jazz at Riverside. That's an error. Oh, it is not? No. There is a listing. It's Big Fat Hand. And they list the number of Steady Roll, but I've checked it with the other Big Fat Hand. And that's what it is. It's not Steady Roll at all. I don't have Steady Roll. I don't know what it is. Well, now, this is... But I think it's unlikely that Morton's on it. I think they're probably right.
